title: max_satisfying() picks rc.9 over rc.10
statement:
Our release tooling picks the wrong release candidate now that we are past rc.9:

    >>> from buildkit.semver import max_satisfying, parse, sort_versions
    >>> max_satisfying(['2.0.0-rc.9', '2.0.0-rc.10'], '>=2.0.0-rc.1')
    '2.0.0-rc.9'          # expected '2.0.0-rc.10'
    >>> parse('2.0.0-rc.10') > parse('2.0.0-rc.9')
    False                 # expected True

Nightly builds sort wrong too: sort_versions(['1.0.0-nightly.20260901.12', '1.0.0-nightly.20260901.3']) leaves .12 before .3. We follow the precedence rules in the buildkit/semver.py docstring (semver 2.0.0, section 11). Please fix ordering everywhere it is used (comparisons, sorting, range checks, max_satisfying) without changing the public API.
